title: Turnrow Profile
description: A single source of truth for a person's professional record, from which a résumé, a LinkedIn profile, schema.org JSON-LD, a slide bio or a Europass CV are generated. Derived from JSON Resume, with an evidence model borrowed from genealogy (GEDCOM 7 / GEDCOM X): every fact carries its sources, competing claims, a confidence level, a review status and a visibility, so nothing unconfirmed or private is ever published by accident.

schemaVersion.description: 2.6.0 adds media assets (versions, renditions, dated person images), other people, recommendations, endorsements and badges; earlier files remain valid.

organizations.description: Organizations defined once and referenced by id everywhere else.

organizationEvents.description: Mergers, acquisitions, spin-offs, splits, renames and rebrands that link organizations over time. Identity is the organization id; names, domains and owners change around it.

places.description: Places defined once and referenced by id (optional; inline places are also allowed).

audiences.description: Named audiences that qualify by relationship (e.g. 'my current employer') and receive only what they are granted. Built-in audiences public, network and private need no entry here.

rules.description: Content rules every rendered output must obey: phrases never to use and statements that are not true (negative assertions). Converters refuse to emit output that breaks a rule.

releases.description: Log of what was released to whom: each entry is a consent receipt for one release. Private; never rendered.

sources.description: The documents facts are drawn from, referenced by id from every citation.

extensions.description: Namespaced data for one consumer, keyed by consumer name (e.g. extensions.linkedin.customUrl).

people.description: Other people, defined once and referenced by id (recommendations, endorsements, references).

id.description: Stable kebab-case id. Never reuse an id for a different fact.

localeTag.description: BCP 47 language tag: en, en-US, es, pt-BR, zh-Hant.

text.description: A string in meta.defaultLocale, or a map of BCP 47 tags to translations.

partialDate.description: ISO 8601 at year, month or day precision: 1973, 2008-08, 2026-11-07.

fuzzyDate.description: A date as precisely as it is known (after GEDCOM date qualifiers). A plain partial date is exact to its precision; the object forms say 'about', 'before', 'after', 'estimated', or 'between' two dates.

visibility.description: public: may appear on the open web. network: signed-in or shared views (LinkedIn, a data room, an application). private: source of truth only; never rendered.

status.description: Review lifecycle. draft: entered, not reviewed. pending: waiting on a named question. approved: the subject (or owner) signed off. disputed: sources conflict and no claim is accepted. retired: kept as history, never rendered.

confidence.description: How sure we are, judged from the evidence (GEDCOM X confidence). Independent of status: an approved fact can still rest only on the subject's word.

evidenceQuality.description: Quality of one citation (after GEDCOM QUAY). primary: an original record made at the time (license, pay record, certificate). secondary: a later record by someone else. selfReported: the subject's own CV, bio or interview. published: press or a third-party profile. hearsay: second-hand, unverified.

quality.description: Overrides the source's defaultQuality for this citation.

quote.description: Short excerpt supporting the claim (keep it brief).

claim.description: One source's version of a field (GEDCOM X evidence vs. conclusion). Keep every competing claim; mark the one the entry uses as accepted.

field.description: The entry field the claim is about, as a dotted path: 'title', 'endDate', 'metrics.marina-slips.value'.

rationale.description: Why this claim was accepted or rejected.

attribution.description: Who changed this entry and when (GEDCOM X attribution). Optional if the file is kept in version control.

lock.description: Set when the subject approves an entry. Any later change must clear the lock and go back for approval (after GEDCOM RESN LOCKED).

entryBase.description: Fields shared by every list entry.

priority.description: Relative weight for short views: a slide bio might take only priority >= 80.

order.description: Explicit display order inside the section; otherwise newest first.

openQuestion.description: What still needs answering. Required while status is pending or disputed.

targets.description: Per-target overrides keyed by target name: { "linkedin": { "title": "…" }, "jsonresume": { "omit": true } }.

audiences.description: Named audiences that may receive this entry even if its visibility would otherwise exclude it (ids from the top-level audiences map).

note.description: Internal note: a ruling, a caveat, where a figure came from. Never rendered in any output or release.

label.description: How the place should read: 'Greater Asheville'.

historicalName.description: The name used at the time, if different: 'British West Indies'.

ids.description: Standard place identifiers, so the place is unambiguous to machines.

placeRef.description: The id of an entry in places, or an inline place.

metric.description: A number that can be confirmed, disputed or hidden on its own.

from.description: When this figure started to apply.

note.description: Internal note: a ruling, a caveat, where a figure came from. Never rendered in any output or release.

orgRef.description: The id of an entry in organizations, or an inline organization.

url.description: Absolute URL, or 'bundle:media/…' inside a profile bundle.

alt.description: Required: describe the image for people who cannot see it.

subjectConsent.description: Record of the subject's consent to publish public entries.

mediaBaseUrl.description: Where the bundle's files are published, ending in /. bundle:media/x.jpg is rendered as <mediaBaseUrl>media/x.jpg; without it, bundle: links are left out of outputs.

script.description: ISO 15924 script code: Latn, Cyrl, Hans.

from.description: When this name came into use (marriage, legal change, transliteration adopted).

pronunciation.description: How to say the name, for directories, introductions and screen readers.

name.description: Display name. Other forms go in names.

pronouns.description: Only if the person chooses to show them.

headline.description: One line: LinkedIn headline, JSON Resume label.

shortBio.description: Two or three lines for slides and cards.

identifiers.description: External ids for the person that are safe to hold (ORCID, a professional license registry). Never put government identity or tax numbers here (SSN, ITIN, passport, driver's license): a profile is meant to be shared, and those numbers should not be in it at all.

additionalProperties.description: A value shaped like a US Social Security or ITIN number (nnn-nn-nnnn) is refused whatever its key.

visibility.description: Visibility of individual person fields (default public). A grant to a named audience still shares a field with that audience.

images.description: Dated portraits. Outputs show the one in force on their date; person.image is used when there are none.

name.description: Display name today. Names over time go in names.

domains.description: Domains the organization controls. A plain string is a current domain; an object can carry dates and a status. Only domains valid on the date of a request qualify a requester, and retired domains never do (they can be bought by anyone).

names.description: Every name the organization has used, with dates: legal names, brands, trade (doing-business-as) names, abbreviations.

identifiers.description: Registry and tax ids, with dates where they changed (tickers and filer numbers end with the entity).

parents.description: Who owned or contained this organization, and when.

note.description: Internal note: a ruling, a caveat, where a figure came from. Never rendered in any output or release.

client.description: Who the work was for, when not the employer.

employerOfRecord.description: Who legally employed and paid you, when different from where you worked (a staffing agency, a PEO, a parent company). Background checks verify against this.

occupations.description: Occupation codes for this work. A responsibility or position may carry its own when it differs from the job's.

service.description: Military, reserve, scouting, volunteer, civic and board service.

occupations.description: Occupation codes for this work. A responsibility or position may carry its own when it differs from the job's.

credential.description: Degree or credential earned. Leave empty for coursework without one.

completed.description: False records study that did not finish in a credential, so no output implies one.

credential.description: Licenses and certifications. credentialId is a real issuer number only, never a note.

active.description: False for lapsed credentials kept as history.

jurisdiction.description: Where a license is valid: US-TX for a Texas PE license or bar admission.

compactStates.description: Other states recognising it under a compact (nursing, telehealth).

aboutPerson.description: True for coverage of the person rather than work by them.

number.description: Patent or report number, e.g. US 11,234,567 B2.

authors.description: Authors or inventors in published order, the subject included.

event.description: A dated life event that is not a job: a journey, a move, a voyage, a first, a founding. Lets the story behind a profile be told the same way everywhere (after GEDCOM events).

relatedTo.description: Ids of work, service or project entries this event belongs to.

reason.description: For career breaks. 'health' is sensitive: keep it private, or describe the break as 'personal'.

media.description: Featured items and evidence files: links, PDFs, images, video. 'bundle:' URLs point inside a profile bundle.

sha256.description: Checksum of the file, so a bundle can be verified.

uuid.description: Stable identity of the photograph or document across re-crops, re-encodes and versions (RFC 9562). sha256 identifies one exact file.

supersedes.description: The media entry this one replaces (an earlier version of the same asset).

focalPoint.description: The point any crop keeps in frame (0–1 from the top left).

license.description: A license URL or an SPDX-style id (CC-BY-4.0).

consent.description: Consent of anyone shown other than the subject.

contentCredentials.description: C2PA Content Credentials: a manifest URL, or embedded in the file.

metadata.description: A few fields read from the file, so a re-export can be matched to its original. Never location.

escoUri.description: ESCO skill URI, for Europass and EU job boards. Prefer codes with system esco; kept for files written before 2.5.

codes.description: Skill, knowledge or software codes (O*NET, ESCO, Lightcast).

reference.description: Private by default; rendered only with the referee's consent.

person.description: The people entry for this referee.

kind.description: forbiddenPhrase: case-insensitive whole words that must not appear. forbiddenPattern: a regular expression that must not match. notTrue: a negative assertion for humans and writing tools (GEDCOM 'NO'); converters also block its phrases if given.

statement.description: For notTrue: the thing that is not true, e.g. 'Does not hold a current captain's license.'

appliesTo.description: Outputs the rule applies to, by their highest included visibility. Default: all.

media.description: Id of the media entry holding the file itself, if it is in the bundle.

location.description: Where the original lives. Never rendered.

url.description: Public address of the source, if it has one.

employerRecord.description: Facts as the employer's own systems record them (title, department, manager, internal ids). The employer is the authority for these fields; they are released only to an audience bound to this job, never to anyone else.

verificationMethod.description: How a requester proves it acts for an organization. oidc/saml: a token from the organization's identity provider. dnsTxt/wellKnown: the organization's domain names the application. signedRequest: signed with a key published at the domain. emailDomain: an address at the domain (weakest; never enough for write-back). invitation: the requester holds a single-use invitation the subject issued.

personGrant.description: A person-level field an audience may receive. personContacts (2.6) also shares the contact details of the other people the release refers to (recommenders, endorsers, references); without it their contacts are withheld.

relation.description: For employer and client audiences: which organizations qualify, resolved from work entries. 'current' follows you to each new job and ends when the job does.

organization.description: A fixed organization, instead of a relation.

workRef.description: Bind the audience to one work entry.

baseVisibility.description: Entries with these visibilities are included; entries naming this audience are included regardless.

person.description: Person-level fields granted. Anything not listed is withheld.

sections.description: Sections the audience may receive (entries still filtered by visibility, status and confidence).

authority.description: Who is authoritative for each field the organization may send back. Employer-authoritative values are accepted unless the entry is locked; subject-authoritative values are kept as suggestions.

organizations.description: Several fixed organizations (a list of funds, say). Any one of them qualifies.

recipients.description: listed: only the organizations named or resolved for this audience. anyVerified: anyone who passes one of the audience's verification methods (a data room with signed invitations, say). anyVerified needs explicit methods and never accepts emailDomain alone.

name.description: Who received it, for anyVerified audiences.

revoked.description: When future syncs were stopped. Copies already delivered remain with the recipient.

organization.description: The organization a rename, rebrand, trade name, reincorporation or dissolution applies to.

predecessors.description: Organizations that stop existing as such (merged, split up).

target.description: For acquisitions and spin-offs: the organization bought or spun off. It keeps its identity.

recordsTo.description: For splits: which successor holds the predecessor's employment records.

name.description: The new name, for renames, rebrands and trade names.

position.description: One title held within a job. A job with several positions is one employer relationship; positions record promotions, re-titles and moves inside it.

officialTitle.description: The employer's title for this position, if it differs.

change.description: How this position began. 'retitle' and 'reorganization' change the name, not the job; 'acquisition' marks titles imposed by a new owner.

level.description: Grade or band, if useful (e.g. L6, Manager II).

reportsTo.description: Title or name of the manager, if appropriate to share.

occupations.description: Occupation codes for this work. A responsibility or position may carry its own when it differs from the job's.

note.description: Internal note: a ruling, a caveat, where a figure came from. Never rendered in any output or release.

media.description: Media for this position only (a badge photo, a project image).

responsibility.description: A duty owned during a job. It can start in one position and continue through promotions and re-titles: its dates (or an explicit list of positions) say when it applied, and outputs show it as continuing.

positions.description: Positions it applied to. If left out, it applies to every position its dates overlap (or the whole job, without dates).

scope.description: Size of the responsibility, which may change over time: give each figure from/to dates (team of 4 in 2019, 12 by 2022).

handedOffTo.description: Who took it over when it ended, if worth noting.

occupations.description: Occupation codes for this work. A responsibility or position may carry its own when it differs from the job's.

note.description: Internal note: a ruling, a caveat, where a figure came from. Never rendered in any output or release.

identifier.description: An identifier issued by a registry or tax authority. Values are stored as issued; formats are checked per scheme. Tax identifiers (ein, stateTaxId) are private unless their visibility or audiences say otherwise.

scheme.description: ein: US Employer Identification Number (IRS), nn-nnnnnnn. Private by default.; uei: US Unique Entity ID (SAM.gov), 12 characters, no I or O, not starting with 0; replaced DUNS for federal awards in April 2022.; duns: D-U-N-S Number (Dun & Bradstreet), 9 digits.; cage: CAGE or NCAGE code, 5 characters (US codes start and end with a digit).; secCik: SEC Central Index Key.; lei: Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442), 20 characters with ISO 7064 check digits.; stateEntityNumber: Secretary of State filing, charter or entity number (Texas file number, Delaware file number, Washington UBI…). Needs jurisdiction.; stateTaxId: State taxpayer, sales-tax or withholding number (Texas taxpayer number, Oregon BIN…). Needs jurisdiction. Private by default.; stateBusinessId: Other state business identifier or license number. Needs jurisdiction.; npi: US National Provider Identifier (healthcare organizations).; ipeds: IPEDS Unit ID (US colleges and universities).; ror: Research Organization Registry id (universities, labs).; wikidata: Wikidata item.; opencorporates: OpenCorporates jurisdiction/company number, e.g. us_tx/0801234567.; companyNumber: National company register number (UK Companies House, etc.). Needs jurisdiction.; vat: EU/UK VAT number, with country prefix.; abn: Australian Business Number.; bn: Canada Business Number, optionally with program account.; siren: France SIREN.; siret: France SIRET (establishment).; ticker: Exchange:symbol, e.g. NYSE:EDS.; isin: ISIN of the organization's listed shares.; figi: Financial Instrument Global Identifier.; other: Anything else; say what it is in label.

jurisdiction.description: ISO 3166-1 country or ISO 3166-2 subdivision that issued it: US, US-TX, GB, CA-ON.

label.description: What the issuer calls it: 'Texas SOS file number', 'Washington UBI', 'Oregon BIN'.

issuer.description: Issuing body, if not obvious from the scheme.

url.description: Public registry page for this record.

visibility.description: Default: private for ein and stateTaxId, public for everything else.

audiences.description: Named audiences that may receive this identifier regardless of its visibility (e.g. an employment-verification audience for an EIN).

occupationCode.description: An occupation code. soc: the U.S. Standard Occupational Classification kept by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (2018 edition, codes like 11-9021). onetSoc: the O*NET-SOC taxonomy built on it (11-9021.00). isco: ILO ISCO-08 unit groups (1323). esco: an ESCO occupation URI. The validator checks soc, onetSoc and their titles against the bundled code lists.

version.description: Edition: 2018 for SOC, 2019 for the O*NET-SOC taxonomy, 08 for ISCO, 2021 for NOC.

label.description: The official title. Filled from the code list when left out.

match.description: primary: the code that best describes the work. secondary: a real part of it (a construction manager who also estimates). related: the nearest code when none fits exactly.

rationale.description: Why this code, when it isn't obvious. Internal; never rendered.

skillCode.description: A skill, knowledge or software code. onet: an O*NET content-model element (2.B.5.b Management of Financial Resources, 2.C.3.d Building and Construction, 2.E.1.e Project management software). esco: an ESCO skill URI. lightcast: a Lightcast Open Skills id. The validator checks onet element ids against the bundled list.

match.description: primary: the code that best describes the work. secondary: a real part of it (a construction manager who also estimates). related: the nearest code when none fits exactly.

otherPerson.description: Someone other than the subject: a recommender, endorser, reference or manager. Every fact is dated; contacts are private by default.

name.description: Display name, as the person is known now.

dateOrDateTime.description: A date, or a date and time with its UTC offset.

scope.description: full: text and name. highlights: only the highlights, with the name. nameOnly: the name and title, no text. anonymous: text per the rest, shown as the author's title only.

by.description: How consent was given (email, form, in person).

recommendation.description: A recommendation someone wrote about the subject, kept verbatim. Private until the author's consent is recorded.

author.description: The people entry of who wrote it.

authorAt.description: Who the author was when they wrote it.

text.description: Must be a verbatim part of text.

capture.description: A media entry: a screenshot or PDF of the original.

endorsement.description: Someone vouching for a skill, credential or badge. Counted only when approved and consented.

target.description: A skills, credentials or badges id.

credential.description: An Open Badges 3.0 EndorsementCredential for this endorsement.

badge.description: A badge or digital credential, described in Open Badges 3.0 terms. The issuer's original credential is kept unaltered in credential.file.

targetFramework.description: O*NET, SOC, ESCO, or another framework's name.

issuerId.description: The issuer profile's URI or DID, as in the credential.

awardedFor.description: The job, course or project it was earned in.

file.description: The original credential, byte for byte (JSON, JWT, or the baked image).

credentialRef.description: The credentials entry this badge represents, so it is counted once.
